title: Carbetocin in comparison with oxytocin in several dosing regimens for the prevention of uterine atony after elective caesarean section in the Netherlands

what_it_measured.text: Carbetocin in comparison with oxytocin in several dosing regimens for the prevention of uterine atony after elective caesarean section in the Netherlands

dose.text: Methods Each of the five participating Dutch hospitals treated 50–100 term patients with 100 μg of intravenous carbetocin on prescription.

route.text: Methods Each of the five participating Dutch hospitals treated 50–100 term patients with 100 μg of intravenous carbetocin on prescription.

Patients Term patients (gestational age C37 weeks) undergoing an elective CS under epidural and/or spinal anaesthesia were treated on physician’s prescription with a single injection of 100 μg of intravenous carbetocin in accordance with the summary of product characteristics (SmPC).
In three hospitals an oxytocin bolus 5 IU was routinely administered, in one hospital an oxytocin bolus 10 IU and in one hospital an oxytocin bolus 5 IU followed by an infusion with 10 IU in 2 h.

endpoint.text: The primary endpoint was the need for additional uterotonic medication.
Primary endpoint was the need for additional uterotonic medication after carbetocin or oxytocin administration.
Secondary endpoints Blood transfusions were administrated in 2.2 % of the cases in the carbetocin group and 2.7 % in the oxytocin group (NS).

reported_results.text: Carbetocin was most effective compared with the oxytocin 5 IU bolus subgroup with less need for additional uterotonic medication (3.1 vs. 9.3 %, p = 0.0067) and blood transfusions (2.2 vs. 3.6 %, p = 0.0357).
Mean number of packed cells per patient was 0.04 versus 0.09 in the carbetocin and oxytocin groups, respectively (p = 0.129).
